title: A Quiet Belly That Is an Emergency

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient is bleeding from an ulcer and has no known coronary disease. A reasonable transfusion threshold is a hemoglobin under about:
questions.explanation: Without cardiovascular disease, transfuse when hemoglobin is under about seven. Use a higher threshold if the heart is already ischemic.

questions.stem: After resuscitation of an ulcer bleed, endoscopy is typically:

options.text: Deferred for a week so the ulcer can heal
Avoided if the albumin gradient is 1.1

questions.explanation: Resuscitate first, then scope, usually within a day.

questions.stem: New ascites. The next procedure is:

options.text: A beta blocker before any fluid is sent
Watchful waiting without a cell count

questions.explanation: New fluid in the belly gets a diagnostic tap.

questions.stem: An ascites neutrophil count of 250 or more means:

options.text: Wait for the culture, then start antibiotics
Start antibiotics now for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, without waiting for the culture

questions.explanation: Neutrophils of 250 or more mean start antibiotics when that count is already present.

questions.stem: An albumin gradient of 1.1 grams per deciliter or more in ascites means:
questions.explanation: A gradient of 1.1 or more means portal hypertension.

questions.stem: Acute pancreatitis is diagnosed by two of three. Antibiotics are:
questions.explanation: Early fluid, feed when pain allows, and antibiotics are not routine.

questions.stem: A stable adhesive small-bowel obstruction. First line is:

options.text: Nasogastric suction and fluids, unless there is peritonitis, a closed loop, or ischemia

questions.explanation: If the patient is stable, suction and fluids come first. An acute belly, a closed loop, or ischemia is an operation.

questions.stem: Severe mid-abdominal pain out of proportion to a soft exam. Lactate is normal. Next test:

options.text: A plain film only, and discharge if it is unremarkable
A contrast angiogram of the mesenteric arteries, and call a surgeon now
Wait for the lactate to rise

questions.explanation: Pain out of proportion is mesenteric ischemia until you prove it is not. Lactate is late. The test is the angiogram.

questions.stem: Suspected variceal bleeding. Immediate medicines include:

options.text: A nonselective beta blocker as the shock treatment
A vasoactive drug and an intravenous antibiotic, then urgent banding

questions.explanation: A vasoactive drug, an antibiotic, and urgent banding. A beta blocker is later prevention, not the treatment of shock.

questions.stem: A nonselective beta blocker in variceal disease is used for:

options.text: Prevention after the bleeding is controlled
Replacing the angiogram in mesenteric ischemia

questions.explanation: The beta blocker is prevention, not the treatment of shock.
